prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1228; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer responded to a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. Driver 1 was stopped in traffic when the vehicle behind them, operated by Driver 2, struck the rear bumper. Driver 2 stated that they did not brake in time, and their account matches the scene. Witnesses at the location described the impact in the same way, and photographs taken at the scene show damage to the rear of Driver 1's vehicle consistent with a collision of this force. Driver 1 reported neck pain and whiplash symptoms and was evaluated at the scene. The injury described is consistent with the mechanics of this type of impact. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of Driver 1's vehicle, and both witnesses and responding officers confirmed Passenger's presence at the time of the collision. Officers found no indication of prior damage to either vehicle. Driver 1 provided proof of insurance listing Driver 1 as the named insured on the policy. Both drivers were cooperative, and no citations were issued at the scene pending further review.
